audience.text: Python developers building applications that require generating Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code barcodes without system-level dependencies.

capabilities.text: Supports Code 128, Code 39 (base and Extended), EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code (Model 2) through dedicated helpers or `generate()`.
capabilities.title: Generate multiple barcode symbologies

capabilities.text: Produce SVG via `to_svg()` and PNG via `to_png()`, with optional `RenderOptions` for scale, DPI, module width, colors, and text display.
capabilities.title: Render barcodes to SVG and PNG

capabilities.text: Control scale, DPI, module width/height, quiet zone, foreground/background color, transparent background, and text font/visibility via `RenderOptions`.
capabilities.title: Customize rendering with RenderOptions

capabilities.text: Implement or use built-in `Renderer` subclasses like `SvgRenderer` and `PngRenderer`, then pass them to `Barcode.render()`.
capabilities.title: Support custom renderer subclasses

capabilities.text: Pass options such as `Code128EncodeMode`, `Code39Options`, `Ean13Options`, `UpcaOptions`, and `QrOptions` to tailor encoding behavior.
capabilities.title: Configure symbology-specific options

capabilities.text: Raise specific exceptions like `BarcodeError`, `EncodingError`, `RenderingError`, `InvalidInputError`, and `SymbologyNotFoundError` for robust error handling.
capabilities.title: Handle errors with typed exceptions

limitations.text: PDF rendering is not implemented; `Barcode.to_pdf()` and `PdfRenderer.render()` raise `NotImplementedError`.
ECI normalization and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions` exposing an `eci_assignment_number` field.
GS1 data parsing and validation are not implemented despite `EncodeOptions` exposing a `gs1_enabled` field.
The library only generates barcodes and does not read or decode existing barcode images.

problems_solved.text: Provides a pure-Python, dependency-light way to generate multiple barcode symbologies with deterministic output.
Enables flexible rendering to SVG and PNG formats with configurable options like scale, DPI, and module width.
Supports both dedicated helper functions and a generic `generate()` entry point for selecting symbologies by name.
Offers structured error handling through dedicated exception types for encoding, rendering, and invalid input.

product_summary.text: Aspose.BarCode FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for generating deterministic, standards-compliant linear and 2D barcodes.

workflows.name: Generate and render a Code 128 barcode
workflows.text: Import `code128`, call it with a payload string, then invoke `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to obtain rendered output.

workflows.name: Generate a QR Code with custom options
workflows.text: Import `qr` and `QrOptions`, configure error correction and encoding mode, then render the result to PNG or SVG.

workflows.name: Add check digit to a Code 39 barcode
workflows.text: Use `code39()` with `Code39Options(add_check_digit=True)` to encode data with an automatic modulo-43 check character.

workflows.name: Render with custom rendering options
workflows.text: Pass `RenderOptions` to `to_svg()` or `to_png()` to control scale, DPI, module width, text visibility, and colors.

workflows.name: Render using a specific renderer instance
workflows.text: Instantiate a `SvgRenderer` or `PngRenderer`, pass it to `Barcode.render()` with `RenderOptions`, and extract rendered data.

workflows.name: Select symbology generically by name
workflows.text: Call `generate(symbology_name, payload)` to produce a barcode for any supported symbology without importing a dedicated helper.
